rows.description: Parents hover, hide news and try to manage everything. Their fear is love. Tell them what help you want and what you want to decide yourself, and reassure them that you can share the hard parts.

rows.description: Some friends disappear because they do not know what to say. It hurts, but it is often discomfort, not lack of care. Tell them how they can help, a simple message or a visit, and cherish those who stay.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, anger, comfort, compassion, fear, protectiveness
related mind states: hurt

rows.description: A friend is ill and you fear saying the wrong thing. Show up, listen more than fix, avoid clichés like everything happens for a reason, and offer specific help such as meals or rides. Presence matters more than perfect words.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, anger, comfort, fear, protectiveness, trust
related mind states: fear, empathy

rows.description: Prayer, ritual or spiritual community brings solace in illness. Let it hold you, and also follow medical advice. Faith and treatment can coexist, and miracle promises that replace treatment are dangerous.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, anger, compassion, fear, protectiveness, trust
related mind states: anger

rows.description: Over time, you learn to live with limits and find what still matters. Acceptance is not surrender; it is choosing how to spend energy and time. Ask for help, redefine goals, and keep dignity and humour where you can.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, comfort, compassion, fear, protectiveness, trust
related mind states: amusement
related concepts: humour

rows.description: Endless deadlines and thanks-free overwork breed bitterness. Signs include cynicism, exhaustion and dread on Sundays. Mature action: talk to your manager about load, take leave, set limits, or change jobs. Silent martyrdom worsens.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, disillusionment, guilt, indifference, neglect, trust
related mind states: gratitude, fear, tiredness, resentment

rows.description: Resting feels lazy, and you keep working while your body pleads. Burnout is a sign of overload, not weakness. Sleep, move, eat, see friends, and get professional help if needed. Productivity built on collapse is not sustainable.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, disillusionment, indifference, neglect, resentment, trust
related mind states: guilt

rows.description: A boss praises your dedication and piles on more. It is a pattern where reliability is punished with load. Document workload, propose priorities, and be ready to say no. Care that costs your health is not worth it.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, disillusionment, guilt, neglect, resentment, trust

rows.description: Your partner has become withdrawn and irritable from overwork. Tell them gently that you miss them, propose small rituals, and encourage rest. Do not take the exhaustion as rejection, and do not enable it silently.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, disillusionment, guilt, indifference, resentment, trust

rows.description: Work has swallowed your evenings and your partner feels alone. Notice it before resentment builds: set a shut-off time, plan a shared day, and be present when home. Ambition without connection becomes hollow.
